questions.q: What separates a heart of peace from a heart of war?
a: Seeing others as people rather than objects
Winning arguments without raising your voice
Avoiding conflict by staying silent
Forgiving people who never apologize
questions.why: Lesson 1 says a heart of war turns people into things, which invites conflict.

questions.q: What did Saladin do after retaking Jerusalem?
a: He spared civilians and let pilgrims pass safely
He executed the city's leaders in revenge
He destroyed the holy sites to end the war
He forced everyone to convert or leave
questions.why: Lesson 1 presents him as an example of choosing peace during war.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest responding to a spouse who skips chores?
a: Listen for the reasons behind their behavior
Point out their unfairness directly
Do the work silently and wait
Ask someone else to confront them
questions.why: Lesson 2 says criticism breeds resistance while understanding invites change.

Believing you are better than everyone else
Believing you are owed special treatment
Believing every conflict is your own fault
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists the victim, better-than and I-deserve boxes.

questions.q: What is the way out of these self-justifying boxes?
a: Try to see the situation from the other person's view
Prove your position with stronger arguments
Withdraw until the other person apologizes
Explain your intentions more clearly
questions.why: Lesson 3 says looking through another's eyes breaks the box's hold.
